metadata.title: ICCS 2022 Technical Report
metadata.venue: IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study 2022

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2022 uses a stratified two-stage cluster sampling design: schools are sampled with probability proportional to size (PPS) and intact classrooms are then randomly selected within schools, with teachers sampled at random within the target grade. The technical report specifies that weighting procedures are used to ensure that results represent the defined student, teacher, and school populations in each participating country, and it distinguishes weighting components for student, teacher, and school surveys. The report also describes the computation of participation rates and standards for sampling participation, and it notes that results are reported separately for countries that meet versus do not meet IEA sample participation requirements to address potential participation bias. For scaling and reporting, the report further describes estimation of sampling variance and imputation variance for civic knowledge scores, including the use of replicate weights for variance estimation (details provided in the weighting/reporting chapters), but the exact weight variable names are not present in the provided excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This technical report documents assessment framework, sampling, weighting, and scaling procedures rather than estimating a student-level predictive model with a specified plausible-values (PV) workflow. While ICCS includes scaling of civic knowledge and questionnaire indices, the excerpt does not provide an explicit PV handling strategy (e.g., Rubin’s rules, PV averaging) or a missing-data handling method for an empirical ML analysis. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are treated as not reported in the context of this extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The target student population is defined as all students in Grade 8 (approximately 14 years of age) provided the average age in Grade 8 is at least 13.5 years; otherwise Grade 9 becomes the target population. The report uses stratified two-stage cluster sampling with PPS school selection and random selection of intact classrooms for the student survey, and it defines the teacher population as teachers teaching regular subjects to the target grade at sampled schools (with an additional section for teachers teaching civic-related subjects). The report also distinguishes reporting based on IEA sample participation requirements: results are separated for countries that meet versus do not meet participation standards, and comparisons across ICCS cycles are restricted to national data points meeting technical standards for sampling, instrument preparation, field operations, scoring, and data management.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2022 is a cross-national study of civic and citizenship education that collects student civic knowledge (via an international test administered on paper or via a computer-based delivery platform), along with student, teacher, and school questionnaires capturing contextual and affective-behavioral constructs. The technical report describes an assessment framework with four civic knowledge content domains and two cognitive processes (knowing; reasoning and applying), plus an attitudes and engagement framework organized into attitudes and engagement constructs. The study uses stratified two-stage cluster sampling: schools are selected with probability proportional to size (PPS) and intact classrooms are randomly selected within schools; principals are nested within sampled schools. Scaling procedures are used to construct civic knowledge scores and questionnaire indices, including equating and mode-effect adjustment when computer-based delivery is used, supported by bridging studies in countries that switched modes. Weighting procedures and variance estimation methods are specified to support population-representative reporting, with results interpreted cautiously for countries not meeting IEA participation standards.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
